title: I made a framework that outperformed DJIA - Open sourced
author: trading_nuts
selftext:
I was a quant researcher at BlackRock so to me the following pipeline is non-negotiable. If it isn't institutional-grade, it isn't deployable. I couldn't find an open-source solution that met that bar, so I decided to go through the pain of building [fintel](https://www.fintel.capital/) myself.

Running agent evals is basically backtesting: simulating how your agent performs over time. Building the agent is easy but evaluating it is the hard part. You have to prevent future data leakage (no peeking past the decision date) and set up serious plumbing - tracing, concurrency, and clean output schemas - to iterate fast enough to find what works.

What you’re seeing here is 5 months of backtesting, where I was confident enough with my [strategy](https://www.fintel.capital/strategy) and threw in 100k USD of my own cash to let my agent do the rest of the work, fully automated. I've wrote a [practical guide here](https://www.fintel.capital/blogs/iterative-agent-improvement) on how it works 

Sharing the base architect for this to demonstrate the edge that fintel could offer, apply with your own strategy, run the evals on your own agent and share the before and after results. 

🔗 **Full docs + architecture :** [**https://github.com/felixdaga/fintel**](https://github.com/felixdaga/fintel)

You bring a **strategy package** (the benchmark), name an **agent**, and fintel runs the simulation under point-in-time data controls — then scores the decisions with the package's KPI.

# What it does

* **Evaluate arbitrary agents** — `djia_strategy_adapter_for_llm_agent` (shipped demo), `openclaw`, `claude-code`, or any `module:Class` adapter you ship.
* **Bring your own benchmark** — a strategy package is the investment strategy: universe, schedule, data surface, mission, output contract, signal, KPI, horizons. The platform never inspects the math.
* **Run controlled backtests** — point-in-time data clamp, per-cell isolation, K-repeat stochasticity, bounded concurrency across cells / dates / repeats.
* **Score post-run** — strategy-dependent metrics, e.g. cross-sectional IC / ICIR, holdings + gross/net NAV, behaviour + output-variance layers, rendered to `report.md`.

  
Feel free to direct message or comment below and share your thoughts and findings, I want to expose this more to the community and see how your trading agent has changed after going through evaluations. Hope this can inspire you!

comments.author: Guegaber
comments.body: very promising. Tks for sharing. Works on MSCI World or S&P 500 as well ?

replies.author: trading_nuts
replies.body: Yes - for systematic the more breath the better so MSCI/ SP500 should work. Tho my set up is one agent per ticker (to ensure output quality) so for each eval period I have 30 agents fired up (DJIA has 30 stocks) independently. For credible backtest u need maybe 20+ periods so u can imagine how much u need to run for SP500 it’s gonna cost you. Advise u try it on a list of 20-30 stocks ur interested in first.
